text: If you trip and fall, pick up a shiny coin from the floor before getting back up—that's Kkaebi's way.
When fierce gales blow, don't fight the storm; unfold your fan and ride the currents.
Never covet golden or silver axes. The plain iron axe fitted to your own grip chops wood best.
Don't despair when a front door slams shut; a mischievous spirit always leaves a rear wall slightly cracked.
Try to please every passing stranger, and even a magical dokkaebi club will shatter from fatigue.
The one who can quietly savor a single cup of tea under moonlight is truly the wealthiest soul alive.
A day that wanders off script might just be a surprise gift box secretly planted by spirits.
The one who extends a hand first does not lose face; they simply take hold of the key to destiny.
Clutching onto autumn's dry leaves leaves you with no free hands to embrace blooming spring flowers.
Turn on the lantern, and fear suddenly looks as ordinary as neatly folded blankets in the corner.
The oldest key on the ring is the one that fits best.
A midnight heart is a hundred times more honest than a daytime greeting.
Regret written in the morning weighs just right for letting go by evening.
Luck always arrives one step after the one who called it.
Laughter is the goblin club’s strongest counter.
